# E0335: ambiguous member type

Two bounds give the type parameter a member of that name. Name the one you mean with a generic, as `C: Collection<T>`, and write `T`.

- Rule: [`traits.member-types`](../../reference/11-traits.md#traits.member-types)
- Reported at: the member type.
- Tier: `advanced`, checked in the `types` phase

## Example

This program makes the mistake:

```stilt E0335:9
trait Collection<Item> {
  fn at(self, i: i64) -> Option<Item>
}

trait Stream<Item> {
  fn next(self) -> Option<Item>
}

fn first<C: Collection + Stream>(c: C) -> Option<C.Item> { None }
```

This one is fixed:

```stilt
trait Collection<Item> {
  fn at(self, i: i64) -> Option<Item>
}

trait Stream<Item> {
  fn next(self) -> Option<Item>
}

fn first<C: Collection<T> + Stream, T>(c: C) -> Option<T> { None }
```

## What the compiler prints

`stilt check` on [`E0335_ambiguous_member_type.lt`](../../tests/diagnostics/E0335_ambiguous_member_type.lt):

```text
── AMBIGUOUS MEMBER TYPE ────────── E0335_ambiguous_member_type.lt:9:50  [E0335]

`C.Item` could be `Collection`'s `Item` or `Stream`'s; name it with a generic,
as `C: Collection<T>`:

  9 │ fn first<C: Collection + Stream>(c: C) -> Option<C.Item> { None }
    │                                                  ^^^^^^

Two bounds give the type parameter a member of that name. Name the one you mean
with a generic, as `C: Collection<T>`, and write `T`.

To fix it, name `Collection`'s `Item` as `T`:

  9 │ fn first<C: Collection<T> + Stream, T>(c: C) -> Option<T> { None }
    │                       +++         +++                  ~
```
